claim.quote: The cross section of the process $e^+e^-\to\pi^+\pi^-$ has been measured in the center of mass energy range from 0.32 to 1.2 GeV with the CMD-3 detector at the electron-positron collider VEPP-2000.

date.locator: arXiv abstract page, submission date (arXiv:2302.08834 v1, 17 February 2023)
date.note: arXiv submission date; published in Phys. Rev. D 109, 112002 (2024). A companion paper, Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 231903 (2024), discusses the muon g-2 implications.

key_value_text.quote: In the dominant $\rho$-resonance region, a systematic uncertainty of 0.7% has been reached.
key_value_text.value: Systematic uncertainty of 0.7% in the dominant rho-resonance region (about 62 pb⁻¹ below 1 GeV)

name: Measurement of the e+e-→π+π- cross section from threshold to 1.2 GeV with the CMD-3 detector
notes: Chosen as the CMD-3 headline result; it is the most precise measurement of this channel by CMD-3 and the one discussed in connection with the muon g-2. The tension between this CMD-3 value and earlier e+e- measurements is not asserted here because the fetched abstracts do not state it.

summary.plain: CMD-3 measured how often electron-positron collisions between 0.32 and 1.2 GeV produce a pair of pions, reaching a systematic uncertainty of 0.7% near the rho resonance. This cross section is a key input to predictions of the muon's anomalous magnetic moment.
summary.technical: CMD-3 at VEPP-2000: e⁺e⁻ → π⁺π⁻ for 0.32 < √s < 1.2 GeV from about 62 pb⁻¹ collected below 1 GeV in three seasons; 0.7% systematic uncertainty in the ρ region; first high-resolution measurement across the φ resonance; the forward-backward charge asymmetry deviates strongly from conventional scalar QED and agrees with generalised vector-meson dominance and dispersion-based predictions (Phys. Rev. D 109, 112002).

title: Measurement of the e+e-→π+π- cross section from threshold to 1.2 GeV with the CMD-3 detector
why_it_matters: The companion paper's title and abstract state that the results bear on the hadronic contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon.
